summary: Unbalanced prefetch timing causing transient GPU starvation and batched latency knees
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a set of dedicated pools (Maply.AI - dedicated) reported sudden P50/P95 latency knees lasting ~2-6 minutes across multiple reservations during peak windows. Impact: customer-facing inference increased P95 by 2-4x and experienced intermittent 429s when client-side retrying caused backpressure.

Impact:
- Affected customer Maply.AI reported degraded SLAs for three live routes (geocode-normalize, route-summarize, labelize) between 08:12-08:20 UTC.
- Traffic patterns show many short, sub-100ms request bursts with prefetch-enabled traffic for long contexts.

Environment:
- Dedicated pools in prod - us-east, GPU family: A100-40GB heterogeneous mix (some older guests with 3xx driver).
- Serving runtime: v2.9.1; Scheduler: v1.4.2; Prefetcher: enabled with default timing window.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) At scale, many small synchronous clients send short requests with prefetch turned on in SDK.
2) Prefetch pipeline issues KV prewarm RPCs with timing skew relative to the main request arrival, creating a wave of prefetch CPU work followed by simultaneous batch attachments.
3) Scheduler assigns fractional GPU slots to many short batches (slot dust) leaving GPUs with many tiny allocations that fail to fully amortize kernel startup.
4) Autoscaler snapshot window interprets the noisy short bursts as transient and delays provisioning, causing short-lived GPU shortages and increased batching latency.

Observed behavior:
- P50 increases modestly but P95/P99 show sharp knees.
- Short-lived 429s and client-side retries correlate with autoscaler backoff traces.
- GPU utilization shows many sub-5% occupancy intervals across nodes while queue depth spikes.

Expected behavior:
- Smooth batching with steady slot occupancy and autoscaler triggering predictable scaling without short starvation windows.

Logs/metrics attached (panels and excerpts included in investigation notes).
comments: 2026-03-13 08:26 - Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged with primary oncall. Customer reports repeated P95 spikes; requested request/response IDs and timeframe. Forwarded logs to SRE.

2026-03-13 08:33 - Oncall (Marcus Huang): Correlated spikes with scheduling logs. Noticed prefetch RPC spikes 100-200ms before main infer RPC. Opening investigation. Slack: #support-dedicated thread INC-20260313-07.
2026-03-13 09:05 - Customer (Maply Ops - Jordan Lee): Confirmed SDK was upgraded last week to enable prefetch=true with default timing window. They can toggle prefetch on a route to test.

2026-03-13 10:12 - SRE (Lena Ortiz): Early mitigation suggestion: disable prefetch for the affected routes on Maply's dedicated pools and observe latency for the next 30 minutes. Asked infra team for quick autoscaler profile adjustment to shorten snapshot window.

2026-03-13 10:45 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer applied prefetch=false on two routes. Reports P95 returned near baseline within ~10 minutes. Requested to keep changes for monitoring while we investigate root cause.
2026-03-14 11:00 - Marcus Huang: Continued investigation; capturing kernel startup traces and autoscaler logs. Planning a controlled repro on staging with mix of small bursts and prefetch enabled.
investigation_notes: 08:20 UTC - Grafana panel (dedicated/us-east/slots): queue_depth spike from 30 to 210 concurrent batches; GPU occupancy per node drops to 3-8% while batch attach rates increase. (panel: /d/dedicated/slot-util)
Scheduler trace: saw 18% of attach RPCs reporting 'prefetch: true' with timestamps 80-220ms earlier than main RPCs for same request IDs (trace samples attached).

Autoscaler logs: snapshot interval=60s; scale decision delayed by 1 interval due to moving-average smoothing. Several nodes entered 'pending-attach' state and were not provisioned before queue spikes hit p99 latency. (log snippet in ticket)

Hypothesis A: Prefetch timing skew produces micro-concurrency that fragments slot allocation and generates many underfilled batches ('slot dust'), reducing effective throughput despite low nominal GPU utilization.

Hypothesis B: Autoscaler smoothing parameter (scale_down/scale_up thresholds) combined with short-lived spikes leads to no immediate provisioning, creating transient GPU shortages even though overall capacity looks sufficient.

Hypothesis C: Heterogeneous GPU set includes a mix with slightly different kernel startup latencies exposed under small-batch heavy attach patterns; the older driver nodes observed higher attach latency but were not preferentially evicted, adding variance.

Evidence: Reproduced similar pattern on staging with 200 client coroutines sending small requests at 50-150 qps with prefetch=true; observed p95 knee and slot dust. When prefetch disabled, pattern disappeared and batching aggregated to larger, more efficient batches.
Related signals: small increase in NVLink attach contention counters and elevation in PCIe retry errors on 3 nodes coincident with spike windows.
action_items: Short-term mitigation: Advise Maply.AI to disable SDK prefetch for affected routes (done) or set prefetch timing window to a higher tolerance (recommendation: 350ms).
Short-term infra mitigation: Reduce autoscaler snapshot smoothing on the specific dedicated pool from 60s to 20s to react faster to short bursts (requires ops change).
Medium-term: Implement prefetch-coalescing in the serving runtime so prefetch RPCs for the same tenant are deduplicated within a 200-400ms window.
Medium-term: Add autoscaler signal from attach-rate (not only queue depth) to detect prefetch waves and pre-provision slots proactively.
Long-term: Add heterogeneous-node-aware placement to prefer nodes with consistent driver/kernel startup for low-batch workloads or route-level allocation preferences.
Monitoring: Add Grafana alert for high queue_depth + low GPU occupancy pattern (queue_depth>150 and avg_gpu_util<10% for 60s) to create early paging alerts for SRE.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13 11:05 - Mitigation applied: Maply disabled prefetch=false for two critical routes. Observed P95 drop to baseline within ~10 minutes. No further 429s reported after 11:20 UTC.

2026-03-13 12:00 - Infra ops adjusted autoscaler snapshot window in staging; validated faster reaction to small bursts in controlled tests. Ops request for permanent config change is filed as INT-48321.

Permanent fix plan: Deliver prefetch-coalescing patch (serving-runtime PR referenced) and autoscaler attach-rate signal by end of Q2. Engineering tickets created and prioritized with product (linked INT-50312, PR: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/4891).
Customer communication: Notified Maply of short-term mitigations and the roadmap items. Customer accepted recommended SDK change and asked to be informed when runtime coalescing is available.
Post-incident: Schedule a postmortem with SRE and Runtime teams to review threshold tuning, prefetch design, and heterogeneous node placement. Tentative postmortem date: 2026-03-20.
customer_feedback: Maply appreciative of quick mitigation; requested guidance on SDK prefetch parameters and a timeline for runtime coalescing. They requested export of per-request traces for their audits.
